mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined monotonically from -17.1% to -13.6% over four weeks, signaling a floor effect where suppressed demand stabilizes. Continued stabilization at this level over the next four weeks will produce no further decline, resulting in higher mean RETAIL_REC relative to the baseline-depressed prior period.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 3.5 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days falls below -14.5%, indicating renewed contraction rather than stabilization.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has recovered from -14.9% to -12.3% (2.6 point gain), indicating partial return of commuting. This workplace recovery will drive weekday retail visits and social activity, lifting RETAIL_REC by 1–2 percentage points over the next two weeks as commuters resume incidental shopping.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 2.6 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES falls below -13.0% in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to the prior two-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has oscillated near zero (-11.1% to -0.9%) over four weeks, indicating suppressed outdoor recreation. If PARKS remains near zero or negative, outdoor substitution for retail will remain weak, and RETAIL_REC will not benefit from weather-driven outdoor-to-indoor switching, keeping it flat or declining.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -0.9% in t-0w, volatile over four weeks
failure_condition: PARKS rises above 5.0% and RETAIL_REC simultaneously increases by more than 2 percentage points over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has remained severely suppressed (-39.4% to -35.3%), indicating persistent mobility restrictions or low confidence in public transport. When TRANSIT falls below -35%, retail-and-recreation venues dependent on transit access experience reduced foot traffic. RETAIL_REC will remain depressed as long as TRANSIT stays below -30%.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -35.3% in t-0w, most suppressed category
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises above -25% while RETAIL_REC remains below -12%, indicating transit recovery is not translating to retail recovery.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 8.0% to 5.6% over four weeks, indicating gradual return to out-of-home activity. The combination of rising WORKPLACES (-14.9% to -12.3%) and falling RESIDENTIAL (8.0% to 5.6%) signals a shift from home-based to activity-based mobility. This dual signal will drive RETAIL_REC upward by 2–3 percentage points as people resume mixed-purpose trips.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises AND RESIDENTIAL falls simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 2.6 points, RESIDENTIAL declined 2.4 points
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL do not move in opposite directions over the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the prior two-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stabilized near -3.4% (declining from -5.3%), indicating essential shopping is normalized. When essential shopping stabilizes, consumers shift discretionary spending to retail-and-recreation. The stabilization of GROCERY_PHARM at low negative levels will free up mobility budget for RETAIL_REC, producing a 1.5–2.5 percentage point gain over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved 1.9 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -5.0% or RETAIL_REC does not improve by at least 1.0 percentage point over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS and RETAIL_REC are jointly suppressed, with PARKS at -0.9% and RETAIL_REC at -13.6%. If PARKS remains near zero or negative over the next four weeks, it signals continued unfavorable conditions (weather, policy, or behavioral) that will also constrain RETAIL_REC. The absence of outdoor-activity recovery will prevent spillover gains to retail.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below 1.0% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:Both PARKS and RETAIL_REC remain suppressed in t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS rises above 3.0% while RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 percentage points, indicating outdoor recovery is not constraining retail.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT remains severely suppressed at -35.3% while WORKPLACES has only partially recovered to -12.3%. This mismatch indicates that workplace access is not fully transit-dependent; however, retail-and-recreation venues in transit-dependent zones will remain inaccessible. When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES diverge (TRANSIT much lower), RETAIL_REC will remain depressed because transit-accessible retail cannot recover.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains more than 20 percentage points below WORKPLACES
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -35.3%, WORKPLACES at -12.3%, gap of 22.9 points
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises to within 15 percentage points of WORKPLACES and RETAIL_REC increases by more than 1.5 percentage points over the next four weeks.
